answer: Meadow-Weighted Prism Split.** Each identity's reward share is the product of a one-time registration fee and a decaying activity gradient sampled across the agent's first N interactions; clones registered in the same window split a single seeded pool rather than each drawing fresh rewards. An attacker cloning k identities pays k fees but captures at most one pool's yield, so marginal clone EV is negative once k exceeds the pool divisor. A drifting ocean of low-cost clones thus dilutes itself faster than it earns.
